VERDICT: EXTEND C0021 | `_run_tool()` timeout handling breaks more than parsing quality: it also corrupts fix-evaluation baselines and verdicts. In `evaluate_fix()`, `_count_tool_issues()` calls runners that return `[]` on timeout parse failure, so pre/post counts become zero and `_compute_fix_verdict()` can label a fix SAFE/NEUTRAL even though no post-fix analysis actually ran. This crosses the endocrine→immune interface because `immune_agents.run_immune_pipeline()` marks findings `verified=True` when `evaluate_fixes()` returns SAFE/NEUTRAL. Timeout-induced empty diagnostics can therefore falsely close bugs. The fix for C0021 should propagate timeout/error status into fix evaluation and treat tool timeouts as UNEVALUABLE, not zero issues.

VERDICT: MERGE C0001 <- F001 | C0001/C0004 are the same root cause: `scan_health()` records tools as available whenever runner returns normally, while runners erase NOT_FOUND into `[]`. Same bug, same downstream effect.

FINDING_ID: F002
SEVERITY: 0.94
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` does not sandbox imports/tests against the copied source tree; it only writes the patched target file to a tempdir under its basename and then invokes tools/tests on that lone file. In `bench/endocrine.py`, `patched_path = os.path.join(tmpdir, os.path.basename(target_path))`, no sibling project files are copied, and `test_cmd` is executed with `cwd=tmpdir` but unchanged arguments. Evidence: pyright/mypy/ruff/bandit on a single isolated file cannot resolve project-relative imports/interfaces the same way as the real tree, and the default immune-stage test command is `["python3", "-m", "pytest", "bench/tests/", ...]`, which from inside `tmpdir` does not point at the repository test tree unless the caller happened to pass absolute paths.
FOLLOW: This undermines the core advertised capability “sandbox-test proposed fixes.” A fix can be marked HARMFUL because isolated analysis creates import/module-not-found errors unrelated to the patch, or marked SAFE because tests never exercised the patched module in repository context. Downstream, `immune_agents.run_immune_pipeline()` trusts SAFE/NEUTRAL to set `verified=True`, enabling NK bug-closed logic and suppressing future findings for that bug. If the sandbox does not mirror the repo, the reviewer gets misleading closure signals and end-to-end verification is wrong.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — copy the full relevant source tree into the temp directory preserving relative paths, write the patched file at its corresponding relative location, and run tools/tests from the temp repo root using the copied paths rather than a lone basename file.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003
SEVERITY: 0.91
FLAW_CLASS: 2
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.61
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `evaluate_fix()` measures “new” tool issues on only the patched file, but executes tests using the unmodified `test_cmd`, so test execution is not coupled to the patched file location. In endocrine.py, post-fix tool counts use `patched_path`, while tests are run as `_run_tool(test_cmd, cwd=tmpdir)`. Evidence: if `test_cmd` contains repo-relative paths like `bench/tests/`, changing only `cwd` to `tmpdir` does not rewrite those paths to the copied sandbox tree; and if `test_cmd` uses absolute paths, tests will run against the real repository, not the patched copy.
FOLLOW: This creates a split-brain sandbox: static checks may inspect the patched temp file while tests inspect either nonexistent paths or the live repo. The verdict can therefore combine post-fix diagnostics from one filesystem with test results from another. That makes SAFE/HARMFUL/NEUTRAL mechanically unsound and can falsely verify fixes in the immune pipeline, again affecting NK dedup closure and human reviewer trust in fix-evaluation results.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — before running tests, rewrite repo-relative file/path arguments in `test_cmd` to point into the temp sandbox root, and reject evaluation as UNEVALUABLE if the command cannot be sandbox-localised.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F004
SEVERITY: 0.86
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.46
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_compute_fix_verdict()` collapses per-tool deltas by summing them: `total_net = net_type + net_ruff + net_bandit`, then treats `total_net > 0` as HARMFUL and `< 0` as SAFE. This allows introduced errors in one tool to be numerically canceled by removed errors in another. Example from the code’s own fields: `net_type_errors=+2`, `net_ruff_errors=-3`, `net_bandit_issues=0` yields `total_net=-1` and verdict SAFE even though the fix introduced new type errors.
FOLLOW: The endocrine layer’s central job is to detect whether a proposed fix breaks anything. Cross-tool cancellation produces silently wrong SAFE verdicts, which `immune_agents` treats as programmatic verification and uses to set `verified=True`. That can close a bug after a fix that actually regresses type safety or security. Because the pipeline is PoC but relies on “first verified fix wins,” this is a high-severity correctness failure.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — mark a fix HARMFUL if any individual net field is positive; only mark SAFE when at least one net field is negative and none are positive.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F005
SEVERITY: 0.83
FLAW_CLASS: 5
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.43
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `_count_tool_issues()` converts any runner exception into `0`, which makes tool execution failure indistinguishable from “no issues found.” In endocrine.py: `except Exception: return 0`. Evidence: this function is used for both pre-fix and post-fix baselines in `evaluate_fix()`, so any internal failure in `run_pyright/run_ruff/run_bandit` silently becomes a clean scan.
FOLLOW: If a tool crashes, times out through an unhandled path, or its parser raises, the fix evaluator sees zero issues and can output NEUTRAL/SAFE instead of UNEVALUABLE. That feeds directly into immune-stage verification and can wrongly mark findings verified. It also hides infrastructure failures from the health monitor, defeating the “whole-body health” function.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — make `_count_tool_issues()` return a distinguished failure result (e.g. `None`) on runner exception, and have `evaluate_fix()` produce verdict `UNEVALUABLE` if any baseline or post-fix tool count failed.
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F006
SEVERITY: 0.74
FLAW_CLASS: 1
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.39
DESCRIPTION: FIND — `compute_pacing_signals()` novelty plateau check ignores the `round_idx` window it claims to evaluate and instead always uses `novelty_counts[-3:]`. If the caller passes a longer history than the current round index represents, the function evaluates future/extra entries rather than rounds ending at `round_idx`. Evidence: current code gates on `round_idx >= 2` but slices the tail of the full list, not `novelty_counts[max(0, round_idx-2):round_idx+1]`.
FOLLOW: Pacing signals are consumed by the insect brain for convergence/timing decisions. Using the wrong rounds can emit or suppress `novelty_plateau` at the wrong time, causing premature convergence checks or missed plateau detection. This does not usually crash the PoC, but it can distort inter-round control flow and reviewer-visible pacing behavior.
PROPOSED_FIX: FIX — compute the recent window from `round_idx` explicitly: use the three entries ending at `round_idx`, and only evaluate when `len(novelty_counts) > round_idx`.
VERIFIED: TRUE
